question: A study group debates cytotoxic T-cell recognition of infected cells. Which claim is accurate?
options: Cytotoxic T cells produce antibodies against bacteria in the blood.
Cytotoxic T cells ignore infected cells and attack only healthy tissue.
T cells recognize pathogens directly without any presentation step.
Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells that display foreign fragments.
gold_answer: Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells that display foreign fragments.
notes: Team-authored original item on cytotoxic T-cell recognition of infected cells. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Cytotoxic T cells ignore infected cells and attack only healthy tissue.

claims.text: A cytotoxic T cell binds only the fragment its receptor matches.

evidence.text: Each T-cell receptor binds a specific peptide-MHC combination, ignoring cells that display other fragments.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes specific receptor binding, which entails the claim.

claims.text: MHC molecules display whole intact pathogens on the cell surface.

evidence.text: MHC molecules display short peptide fragments, not whole intact pathogens.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states fragments, not whole pathogens, are displayed, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: The trial tested a T-cell therapy in patients with one cancer type.

claims.verdict_rationale: One cancer type cannot support cures for every cancer, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells that display foreign fragments.

claims.text: Bound cytotoxic T cells trigger death of the infected target cell.

evidence.text: After recognition, the T cell releases perforin and granzymes that drive the infected cell into programmed death.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes target-cell killing after recognition, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Cytotoxic T cells recognize free-floating virus particles.

evidence.text: T cells recognize fragments displayed on cell surfaces, while free particles are handled by antibodies.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns free-particle recognition to antibodies, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Receptor sequences were sampled from donors in the repertoire study.

claims.verdict_rationale: Sampling sequences cannot show all receptors are identical, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Cytotoxic T cells produce antibodies against bacteria in the blood.

claims.text: Infected cells display pathogen fragments on MHC class I molecules.

evidence.text: Nearly all nucleated cells load peptide fragments onto MHC class I molecules for surface display, including fragments from intracellular pathogens.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes fragment display on MHC class I, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Helper T cells kill infected cells directly.

evidence.text: Helper T cells coordinate the response with signals, while the direct killing is carried out by cytotoxic T cells.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns direct killing to cytotoxic cells, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Vaccines work without any T-cell involvement.

evidence.text: T-cell responses were measured as a secondary endpoint in the vaccine trial.

claims.verdict_rationale: Measuring responses does not show vaccines work without them, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
